answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a small bond that only matures after a history of useful work, so a whisper of fake accounts cannot flood the market cheaply. Like a willow that bends yet holds its roots, reputation should grow slowly from verified interactions and decay when an agent goes idle. New entrants start in a shared garden of low-trust tasks, earning their way into higher-value work only through consistent, auditable performance, so each clone pays the full cost of a real history.
